title: Crime Reporting and Police Controlling: Mobile and Web-Based Approach for Information-Sharing in Iraq
authors: T. Alameri; A. H. Alhilali; N. S. Ali; J. K. Mezaal
abstract/content snapshot: The proposed mobile application keeps witness reports undisclosed and sends location, case type and time to police. A web control module validates reports, displays confirmed cases on a colour-coded crime map and tracks suspects through a cloud database. This combines anonymous reporting, GPS geolocation, community validation and direct police integration.

title: A Cloud-Based Crime Reporting System with Identity Protection
authors: T. Shih; C. Chen; B. Syu; Y. Deng
abstract/content snapshot: This cloud reporting system protects identity confidentiality with a cryptographic mechanism. Authentication, encrypted messages and privacy preservation allow a witness to submit an anonymous report while authorized law enforcement can verify required information.

title: An Android Location-Based Crime Reporting System Using the Google Map API
authors: M. Timothy
abstract/content snapshot: The Android system coordinates Google Maps and Places APIs to report a crime to a nearby police station. GPS geolocation, map display, app-to-app calls, audio recording and image evidence provide multimedia reporting and law enforcement integration.

title: Crime Reporting System for University of Energy and Natural Resources
authors: A. Vivian; E. A. Obeng
headings separated by ||: Introduction||Literature Review||Proposed System||Research Method||Testing and Results||Discussion||Conclusion
abstract/content snapshot: The campus application reports online with GPS and offline through SMS where internet is unavailable. It sends reports to security and police, provides emergency contacts, uses Firebase authentication and end-to-end encryption, and lets administrators locate a reporter on Google Maps.

title: Android Based Crime Reporting System Using Firebase
authors: R. Dhinakaran; R. Ambikapathy
abstract/content snapshot: This online Android system uses Firebase to let the public submit crime reports and check the status of a reported crime. Police integration gives officers the submitted information while case status tracking returns investigation updates to users.

title: Crime Reporting App Using Android Application System
authors: P. Khambalkar; S. Kalwale; M. Ramteke; S. D. Zade
abstract/content snapshot: The Android crime reporting application replaces manual records with a secure computerized system. Authentication and access control give the organization fast access to stored reports and reduce duplicate entries.

title: Crime Reporting System Using Android Application
authors: S. P. Godlin Jesil; R. Basant; Pratishvir
abstract/content snapshot: The Android application makes criminal information available through cloud storage and connects citizen reporting with the police department. Registered user authentication supports report submission and law enforcement integration, while the records can be updated during an investigation.

title: Impact of Crime Reporting System to Enhance Effectiveness of Police Service
authors: K. N. Jayasinghe; M. P. L. Perera
abstract/content snapshot: This review studies how online crime reporting systems close the gap between reported and unreported crime. It emphasizes public involvement, privacy and security, access to law enforcement, and how digital reports can assist ongoing police investigations.

title: When Crime Reporting Goes High-Tech: An Experimental Test of Computerized Citizen Response to Crime
authors: D. G. Gilling; J. W. Wilson
abstract/content snapshot: A randomized experiment compares telephonic reporting with a computer-interactive crime reporting mode. The computerized two-way interaction increased citizen reporting rates for incidents of low and moderate seriousness.

title: Development of Crime and Incident Reporting Mobile Application with SMS Notification
authors: J. M. Gallera
abstract/content snapshot: The application accepts anonymous reports with pictures, video and text, geotags the incident and forwards it to the nearest police station. A police dashboard manages incidents, while SMS sends real-time status tracking notifications to the reporter and law enforcement.

title: Mobile Application for Crime Recognition System
authors: S. Chaudhari; S. Jain; M. Shaikh; R. Jadhav
abstract/content snapshot: The smart-city Android application allows posting an incident, searches crime by location and displays crime places on a Google map. An SOS panic button, emergency numbers and high-alert safety notifications connect users with police, who verify shared incidents through community validation.

title: A Proposed Solution for Crime Reporting and Crime Updates on Maps in Android Mobile Application
authors: S. M. Raza; L. Rajamanickam
abstract/content snapshot: The Android proposal shows crime locations on a map, gives neighbourhood safety alerts and lets the public report evidence to law enforcement. Police database integration and communication support current crime updates, while validation recommendations address fake reports.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: K. He; X. Zhang; S. Ren; J. Sun
abstract/content snapshot: Residual neural networks use shortcut connections to train substantially deeper models for image recognition. Experiments compare architectures on ImageNet and CIFAR datasets and report classification accuracy.

title: Attention-Based Neural Machine Translation
authors: D. Bahdanau; K. Cho; Y. Bengio
headings separated by ||: Abstract||Introduction||Related Work||Neural Machine Translation||Learning to Align and Translate||Experimental Settings||Results||Conclusion
abstract/content snapshot: An attention mechanism allows a neural translation model to align source and target words without compressing an entire sentence into one fixed vector. Translation experiments compare results with baseline systems.

title: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
authors: O. Ronneberger; P. Fischer; T. Brox
abstract/content snapshot: A U-shaped convolutional architecture combines a contracting path with precise localization for biomedical image segmentation. Data augmentation permits effective training from limited annotated images.

title: Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Sequence Modelling
authors: A. Graves
headings separated by ||: Abstract||Introduction||Background||Model Architecture||Training Procedure||Experimental Setup||Results and Discussion||Conclusion
abstract/content snapshot: Recurrent neural networks with long short-term memory units learn temporal dependencies for sequence modelling. The evaluation uses speech and handwriting datasets and describes training settings.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Data Synthesis
authors: I. Goodfellow; J. Pouget-Abadie; M. Mirza
headings separated by ||: Abstract||Introduction||Related Work||Adversarial Nets||Theoretical Results||Experiments||Advantages and Disadvantages||Conclusions and Future Work
abstract/content snapshot: A generator and discriminator are trained in an adversarial process. Experiments demonstrate learned representations and synthesized samples while theoretical analysis describes the equilibrium.

title: Transformer Models for Language Understanding
authors: A. Vaswani; N. Shazeer; N. Parmar
abstract/content snapshot: The Transformer uses self-attention rather than recurrence or convolution. Machine translation experiments describe model architecture, optimization, regularization, results and comparisons with previous systems.

title: Graph Neural Networks: Methods and Applications
authors: Z. Wu; S. Pan; F. Chen
headings separated by ||: Abstract||Introduction||Related Work||General Design Pipeline||GNN Models||Applications||Datasets and Open-Source Codes||Future Directions||Conclusion
abstract/content snapshot: This survey organizes graph neural network architectures, applications and benchmark datasets. It compares methods and identifies limitations and future research directions.

title: Deep Learning for Time-Series Forecasting
authors: H. Ismail Fawaz; G. Forestier; J. Weber
headings separated by ||: Abstract||Introduction||Literature Review||Datasets||Data Preprocessing||Proposed Method||Experimental Setup||Results||Comparison with Baselines||Limitations||Conclusion
abstract/content snapshot: A review and experimental study evaluates deep neural architectures for time-series classification. Standard datasets, preprocessing, evaluation measures and baseline comparisons support reproducible results.

title: Explainable Deep Learning in Medical Diagnosis
authors: S. Tjoa; C. Guan
abstract/content snapshot: The journal survey presents a taxonomy of explainability methods for deep medical models. It reviews datasets, evaluation metrics, clinical limitations and research opportunities.

title: EfficientNet: Scaling Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: M. Tan; Q. Le
headings separated by ||: Abstract||Introduction||Related Work||Compound Model Scaling||EfficientNet Architecture||Experimental Setup||Results||Ablation Study||Discussion||Conclusion
abstract/content snapshot: A compound coefficient scales network depth, width and resolution. Image classification experiments compare EfficientNet with baseline convolutional networks and include ablation studies.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Control
authors: S. Levine; C. Finn; T. Darrell
abstract/content snapshot: A deep reinforcement learning method learns visuomotor policies for robotic manipulation. The paper details data collection, training, experiments, results and practical limitations.

title: BERT: Pre-training Deep Bidirectional Transformers
authors: J. Devlin; M. Chang; K. Lee; K. Toutanova
headings separated by ||: Abstract||Introduction||Related Work||BERT Architecture||Pre-training Tasks||Fine-tuning Procedure||Experiments||Ablation Studies||Results||Conclusion
abstract/content snapshot: A bidirectional Transformer is pre-trained on unlabelled text and fine-tuned for language tasks. Experiments report benchmark results, implementation details and ablation studies.
